phenotypes.hpo_label: Recurrent infection of the gastrointestinal tract
Decreased specific antibody response to unconjugated polysaccharide vaccine

phenotypes.text: defective in vitro plasma cell differentiation

records.segregation: perfectly segregated with the disease within Family I; linkage peak LOD 3.31 on chromosome 3
quotes: We investigated 10 individuals in Family I (Figure 1A), who had antibody isotype deficiencies involving IgM, IgG and IgA (Table S1) and who suffered from severe recurrent bacterial infections such as tonsillitis, otitis, sinusitis, pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections.
By Sanger sequencing we confirmed that the heterozygous missense mutation (c.254T>A, p.V85D) in SEC61A1 perfectly segregated with the disease within Family I (Figure 1B).
Affected individuals did not respond to polysaccharide vaccination and responded variably to tetanus toxin vaccination (Table S1).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: II.P3

phenotypes.text: defective in vitro plasma cell differentiation

records.segregation: mother and grandmother (II.P1) also carry the mutation
quotes: The index patient of Family II (Figure 1A) was an eight year old boy who had hypogammaglobulinemia since birth but owing to IVIG treatment has not experienced any severe or recurrent infections
We identified a heterozygous nonsense mutation (c.1325G>T, p.E381*) in individual II.P3 from Family II (SIFT score: 0.003).
His mother (who is affected by a secondary immunodeficiency and therefore not included in this study) and grandmother (II.P1) are also mutation carriers
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

records.label: II.P1

phenotypes.text: increased frequency of upper respiratory infections in childhood

records.segregation: mutation carrier; grandmother of index patient
quotes: the latter reported an increased frequency of upper respiratory infections during childhood with recurrent bilateral bacterial otitis media. Now, at age 66, she has normal immunoglobulin serum levels (Table S1).
records.genotype_reason: single heterozygous variant; mode as stated for the family

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) carried out a genome-wide linkage analysis in Family I and found linkage to chromosome 3 between markers D3S3697 and D3S3684. The peak LOD score was 3.31.
quotes: The peak single-marker and multiple-marker LOD score was 3.31. The genetic linkage analysis established that the mutated gene should be between markers D3S3697 and D3S3684 (Table S2).

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) ran targeted sequencing of SEC61A1 in more than 200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency and found a nonsense mutation in 1 of them. The gnomAD database listed no premature stop mutations in SEC61A1 in healthy individuals.
quotes: Seeking additional individuals with SEC61A1 mutations, we performed targeted next generation sequencing in >200 additional patients with primary antibody deficiency.
there are no mutations reported in healthy individuals leading to a premature stop codon in SEC61A1.

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found reduced SEC61A1 protein in naive B cells from carriers of the E381* mutation, and no truncated protein was detected. They concluded that the nonsense mutation likely causes nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency.
quotes: supporting the hypothesis that the nonsense mutation p.E381* likely results in nonsense-mediated mRNA decay and leads to SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency in Family II.

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found that purified B cells from mutation carriers in both families showed significantly reduced in vitro differentiation into plasmablasts and plasma cells and secreted less IgG and IgA. EBV-transformed B cell lines from patients lacked the CD38-high/CD138-positive plasma cell subpopulation and secreted less immunoglobulin.
quotes: The differentiation of resting peripheral B cells into CD27+CD38high plasmablasts and CD38highCD138+ plasma cells was significantly decreased in mutation carriers from both families upon T cell dependent (Figure 3A, B) and T cell independent (Figure S2A, B) stimulation.
Intriguingly, we observed that all HD cell lines contained a subpopulation of CD38highCD138+ plasma cells that was absent in all patient-derived cell lines (Figure 4C).

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found that the V85D mutation impaired cotranslational translocation of preprolactin in HeLa cells. Overexpressing it lowered the ER calcium load, which they took to be a dominant effect from increased calcium leakage through the channel.
quotes: We observed that co-translational transport of ppl through the SEC61A1-V85D channel was significantly decreased compared to the transport through the wt channel (Figure 5B).
we conclude that the effect on the ER/cytosol Ca2+ gradient is a dominant effect of SEC61A1-V85D.

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) found that stable expression of SEC61A1 V85D caused GFP-positive cells to disappear from multiple myeloma cell lines but did not affect other cell lines. In myeloma cells it activated the terminal unfolded protein response, with upregulation of PERK, ATF4 and CHOP.
quotes: Taken together, these observations indicate that SEC61A1-V85D production selectively impairs the survival of plasma cell lines.

In addition to XBP1s, mRNA levels of ATF4 and CHOP were upregulated upon SEC61A1-V85D overexpression in L-363 cells (Figure 7C), pointing to the activation of the terminal UPR in this plasma cell line.

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) suggested that SEC61A1 haploinsufficiency causes possibly transient hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in Family II. In contrast, the dominant-negative V85D mutation may underlie the fully penetrant antibody deficiency in Family I, which ranged from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.
quotes: We suggest that SEC61A1 haploinsufficincy is causing (possibly transient) hypogammaglobulinemia with variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance in Family II.
may be responsible for the fully penetrant PAD in Family I ranging from transient hypogammaglobulinemia and specific antibody deficiency to CVID.

notes.statement: Schubert et al. (2018) noted that SEC61A1 is a target gene of XBP1s. By proteomics, SEC61A protein was about 2-fold more abundant in human peripheral blood plasmablasts than in naive and memory B cells.
quotes: As determined by mass spectrometry-based proteomics, the relative abundance of SEC61A protein is two-fold higher in plasmablasts from human peripheral blood as compared to naïve and memory B cells (Figure 1E).

notes.statement: Taubenheim et al. (2012) found that antibody-secreting cells were generated efficiently in the absence of XBP-1 in vitro and in vivo, occurring at normal frequencies in resting and immunized mice with typical plasma cell surface markers; XBP-1 deficiency reduced but did not ablate antibody secretion and prevented development of the characteristic plasma cell morphology. They concluded that plasma cell differentiation can proceed relatively normally without high rates of Ig secretion.
quotes: Using both in vitro and in vivo assays, we found efficient generation of ASCs in the absence of XBP-1. ASCs were present at normal frequencies in resting and immunized mice and displayed a pattern of surface markers typical for plasma cells.
The absence of XBP-1 resulted in a reduction but not ablation of Ab secretion and the failure to develop the cellular morphology characteristic of ASCs.

notes.statement: Reimold et al. (2001) found that mouse lymphoid chimeras deficient in Xbp1 had normal numbers of activated B lymphocytes that proliferated, secreted cytokines, and formed normal germinal centers. However, the chimeras secreted very little immunoglobulin of any isotype and failed to control infection with the B-cell-dependent polyoma virus, because plasma cells were markedly absent.
quotes: Mouse lymphoid chimaeras deficient in XBP-1 possessed normal numbers of activated B lymphocytes that proliferated, secreted cytokines and formed normal germinal centres.
However, they secreted very little immunoglobulin of any isotype and failed to control infection with the B-cell-dependent polyoma virus, because plasma cells were markedly absent.

notes.statement: Reimold et al. (2001) found that XBP1 transcripts were rapidly upregulated in vitro by stimuli that induce plasma cell differentiation and were present at high levels in plasma cells from rheumatoid synovium. Introducing XBP1 into B-lineage cells initiated plasma cell differentiation. The authors concluded that XBP1 is the only transcription factor known to be selectively and specifically required for the terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes into plasma cells.
quotes: XBP-1 transcripts were rapidly upregulated in vitro by stimuli that induce plasma-cell differentiation, and were found at high levels in plasma cells from rheumatoid synovium.
When introduced into B-lineage cells, XBP-1 initiated plasma-cell differentiation.
XBP-1 is the only transcription factor known to be selectively and specifically required for the terminal differentiation of B lymphocytes to plasma cells.
